description:
We are a pair of twins who are very passionate about space and technology.

Our goal is to make simple things with technology, that help others be more related with space and science.
summary:
We developed a digital library, we believe that this addresses the challenge in a way that it helps teens and classrooms learn about the spacecraft talked about in the books, in a more fun an dynamic way since they can interact with the books, with an interactive quiz that gives them a score based on their answers, a color by number page at the end of each book. And also an audiobook option with auto-turn for each page.

We believe that teaching should also be fun, so we made our site in a way that it fits for schools and, can be used as a teaching tool, to help students engage more with the stories and use the site as a way to play and have fun while they still get to learn new things.
details:
Our project was made with the purpose of helping students learn more about space, spacecraft and their stories, while being able to have fun with interactive quizzes. It contains a library with four different books about spacecraft abandoned in the Moon and Mars, each book has an audiobook version and auto-turn part after the narrator finishes reading each page, each book has a quiz in the last page that consists of two rounds with 5 randomized questions each, there is also a color by number page in each book, where the reader will be able to color the spacecraft that the book talks about. There is also a timeline and a map where anyone is able to see the location of these spacecraft on Mars or the Moon. We also added an animation at the start, where Neil Armstrong is shown walking out of Eagle and planting the U.S. flag. 

TOOLS USED & TECHNOLOGIES USED:

Website

  • Languages: HTML, CSS and JavaScript. No frameworks or outside code libraries; everything is written from scratch.
    • Canvas 2D: pixel art, the coloring page, the maps and the intro animation
    • Web Audio API: the ambient sound and the intro’s sound effects, generated live
    • Media Session API: audiobook controls on the phone’s lock screen
    • Local storage: remembers language, sound setting and best quiz scores

Fonts (both free, from Google Fonts)

  • Press Start 2P: titles and headings
  • VT323: body text
  • Demo video: a Minecraft-style pixel font from CapCut’s built-in font library

AI

  • Claude (by Anthropic), used through the Claude Code desktop app: coding, research simplification, generated sounds and music, the demo’s ending screen and the QR code
  • Google Translate: first draft of the Spanish stories, reviewed and corrected by us

Demo video

  • Recording: iPad screen recording
  • Editing: CapCut
  • Transfer: Google Drive, to move files between laptop and iPad
  • Hosting: YouTube

NASA data sources

  • NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDC)
  • science.nasa.gov

HOW WE USED AI:

We used Claude (by Anthropic), through the Claude Code desktop app, as a coding and writing assistant.

  • Research: We gave Claude official NASA mission data (NSSDC, science.nasa.gov), and it helped us turn the technical language into simpler explanations that we used as a factual base.
  • Stories: All stories were written by us, in our own words.
  • Narration: All English and Spanish narration was recorded by Camila. No AI voices were used.
  • Translation: The Spanish stories were translated with Google Translate and then reviewed and corrected by us as native speakers. Claude helped translate the “Our mission” page.
  • Pixel art: We designed the spacecraft pixel art ourselves as drafts, and Claude turned our designs into code so they could be drawn on the website.
  • Website code: Claude wrote the HTML, CSS and JavaScript based on our design direction and content: the book reader, quiz, coloring page, map, timeline and the opening animation of Neil Armstrong’s first step.
  • Sounds and music: The website’s ambient sound, the intro’s sound effects and the music in our demo video were generated by code written by Claude. No songs or sound libraries were used. The audio files are in our GitHub repository, in audio/claude-generated.
  • Demo video: We recorded and edited the video ourselves. Claude made the ending screen with the QR code.
